## Cost analysis

Current-live task202 is a compact stripe/zero-marker extension graph using per-color row/column presence, orientation scoring, and final `Where` to zero active line cells. The dominant cost is intermediate memory from repeated per-color `[1,1,30,30]` boolean/float masks (`And`, `Cast`, `ReduceSum`, `Greater`) rather than params. Return follow-up `t_f3a0e88b` found a larger structural-only exact-current-live shrink: for valid NeuroGolf one-hot inputs the full fixed 30x30 tensor is active (background padding included), so the graph's active extent is constant 30 and the final active line gate is redundant. Combining that const30 rewrite with `GreaterOrEqual` reduces cost to 156881 (-16278, +0.098723 pts) with visible candidate-vs-LIVE 230/230 and 5000 seeded random valid one-hot exact checks. It is preserved as no-submit/fallback evidence because the earlier reviewer-approved fp16/no-active candidate is much stronger at cost 130363.

The 2026-05-17 canonical package already superseded those stale-baseline numbers with `task202_current_live_shrink_t_f2425e39` at cost 148049. Rechecking the same valid-one-hot invariant on that current canonical model found a remaining final `active` gate (`ReduceSum(input)>0.5` and `And(line_any, active)`) that is still redundant for every valid fixed 30x30 NeuroGolf tensor. Removing only that gate gives `task202_t25208314_no_final_active_gate` at cost 142649, a current-live improvement of -5400 cost / +0.037156 points, with only `task202.onnx` changed in the staged package and exact current-live equivalence on 230 supported visible cases plus 5000 random valid one-hot cases.

Return follow-up `t_b05e23ce` found a stronger exact successor on the same current canonical base. Beyond the active-gate removal, the horizontal orientation calculation can use one variadic `Sum` over the nine row-present floats instead of an 8-output `Add` chain, and the vertical black-column masks can multiply `ch0` by `col_countN` directly instead of by `Cast(col_presentN)` because the downstream `ReduceSum > 0.5` check only distinguishes positive from zero. This drops cost to 140729 (-7320 / +0.050707 points vs current canonical), just over the standalone +0.05 floor, while staying exact against the current canonical model on all 230 supported visible cases and 5000 seeded random valid one-hot tensors.
